summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma, was admitted with left lower quadrant abdominal pain, profuse watery diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting. His symptoms were similar to a prior C. difficile infection. CT imaging showed no acute abdominal process, colitis, or obstruction, with findings consistent with stable post-cholecystectomy changes and cirrhosis. He was started empirically on oral metronidazole for suspected recurrent C. difficile colitis. His symptoms improved, he tolerated a diet, and stool testing confirmed C. difficile. He remained stable with no liver decompensation, continued on home medications, and was discharged home on a full 14-day course of metronidazole with instructions for a bland diet and follow-up.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis
Other and unspecified alcohol dependence, in remission
Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Malignant neoplasm of liver, not specified as primary or secondary
